runs.text: Welcome your reader in, then hand them your thesis

slides.notes: Today students begin, and some finish, their introductions, which end with their thesis statement. Before you start: everyone who has been in class should have a working thesis (absent students can catch up). The thesis is the first real milestone, and once it works the essay almost writes itself. Celebrate it; have a few students share theirs aloud or with a partner.

A good thesis statement is easy for the reader to agree with.
A good thesis statement contains 2–3 pieces of support.
A good thesis statement contains observation and analysis.
A good thesis statement contains research and facts.
A good thesis statement is 1–2 sentences long.

Welcome your reader into your discussion and state the thesis

runs.text: Place the following 7 terms in order:

slides.notes: Individually, in pairs or in teams. The instructions are deliberately vague. If they ask "what order?", just say "an order that works." Don’t tell them it’s largest to smallest. Most get there fast (smallest to largest works too); the odd one will go alphabetical.

runs.text: Place the following 7 terms in order:

slides.notes: Ask why they chose that order. Brian’s Google Earth picture: type in an address and it starts you out in space, then zooms to the planet, the continent, the country, the state, and down into the neighborhood. Boop: there’s your address. That is the mentality for an introduction.

runs.text: Place the following sentences in order:
Across these movies, Iron Man is sometimes portrayed as arrogant, self-centered, elitist, and reckless.
One of those relationships is with Pepper Potts, and the other is with Peter Parker’s Spider-Man.
Iron Man is featured in 9 MCU movies.
However, two relationships help him develop less selfish and more human qualities.
There are 29 movies in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

slides.notes: Read the five sentences aloud so everyone is together. Students only need to write the numbers, not the sentences. They usually need a minute or two.

runs.text: Broad to specific, one thread at a time
There are 29 movies in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
Iron Man is featured in 9 MCU movies.
Across these movies, Iron Man is sometimes portrayed as arrogant, self-centered, elitist, and reckless.
However, two relationships help him develop less selfish and more human qualities.
One of those relationships is with Pepper Potts, and the other is with Peter Parker’s Spider-Man.

slides.notes: Have a team share, then break it down: very broad (29 movies) to very specific (two relationships). Point out that each sentence reaches up to the one above and brings down a thread: nine of those 29; across these nine; however, two relationships; one of those two. Each one logically leads to the next. That is what their introduction will do.

runs.text: Now you can begin writing your essay.

slides.notes: Reinforce it: never start writing an essay until you have your thesis statement. Now they can.
A very nice place to start.

runs.text: prepare them to understand your thesis statement.

slides.notes: That’s it. We would never begin with the thesis: it’s too complex. Tell students their theses are so beautiful and pack such a punch that the reader needs to be prepared for them. There’s a handout in the resources with the next few slides on it.

runs.text: Story or example that illustrates your topic

slides.notes: Four options. All four examples that follow end on the same thesis, the one from the sample essay. Make sure students know they will write their own intro today; raising the stakes helps them pay attention to the examples.

runs.text: EXAMPLE INTRODUCTION · THE THESIS IS IN ITALICS

Ms. Rodriguez watches as 28 ninth graders stare blankly at their worksheets, the only sound the fluorescent lights humming overhead. She had once dreamed of inspiring young minds, but now finds herself mechanically walking through the same lesson plan she's used for five years. In the back row, students doodle in their notebooks and struggle to stay awake. Throughout the school, teachers click through PowerPoint slides and tell students to stop talking, while kids daydream and stare at the clock. This scene plays out in classrooms across the country, where both educators and students have lost the spark that should define learning. This may be because schools have lost a sense of what really works in terms of motivating students to learn.
When schools fail to prioritize creativity in teaching, school becomes boring for both students and teachers, resulting in a lack of shared motivation, excitement, and accomplishment.

slides.notes: Read it aloud, or have a student read it. A story or scene feels like a story: description, maybe a character, even dialogue. It brings the reader into a shared scene you can refer back to later, and it gives a really good example of the thing you’re talking about. Point out that it starts general and narrows, and that the thesis (in italics) is the last sentence. If you used a different sample essay, consider writing your own example of each style that ends on that essay’s thesis.

runs.text: EXAMPLE INTRODUCTION · THE THESIS IS IN ITALICS

Do you remember trying to learn how to ride a bike? It was exciting, blood rushing, and challenging, but worth it. When you got going but fell, you got back up and went a little further each time. You had more motivation to keep going because it was exciting. Schools today seem to lack this sense of excitement. Students have zero motivation to keep going because there is no excitement from the teachers and no sense of an end goal for the students. Shouldn't the process of learning be inspiring and exciting for everyone?
When schools fail to prioritize creativity in teaching, school becomes boring for both students and teachers, resulting in a lack of shared motivation, excitement, and accomplishment.

slides.notes: Define it. Most students will say a rhetorical question is one that isn’t supposed to be answered. True, but the real idea: the writer asks it so they can supply the answer they want the reader to hear. Haley asks about learning to ride a bike, then answers: exciting, blood rushing, challenging, but worth it. That answer is exactly what she wants us to believe school should be.

runs.text: EXAMPLE INTRODUCTION · THE THESIS IS IN ITALICS

Albert Einstein once said, “It is the supreme art of the teacher to awaken joy in creative expression and knowledge.” But walk into most American classrooms today and you'll find the opposite: students mechanically filling out worksheets while teachers follow rigid scripts designed to meet testing requirements. The joy Einstein spoke of has been replaced by compliance and conformity. Both students and educators go through the motions of learning without the spark of curiosity or discovery that should drive education.
When schools fail to prioritize creativity in teaching, school becomes boring for both students and teachers, resulting in a lack of shared motivation, excitement, and accomplishment.

slides.notes: A relevant quote is a strong opener. If students are writing about a book, article or essay, a quote from that text is a great start; teach the TAG method (title, author, genre) to set it up: "In the essay The American Scholar, Ralph Waldo Emerson states…"

runs.text: EXAMPLE INTRODUCTION · THE THESIS IS IN ITALICS

Education, by definition, is the process of facilitating learning, or the acquisition of knowledge, skills, values, and habits. This definition suggests an active, dynamic exchange between teacher and student—a collaborative journey of discovery and growth. However, in many of today's classrooms, education has become something far more mechanical: the transfer of standardized information from textbook to test, with little regard for genuine understanding or intellectual curiosity. Students sit in rows, passively receiving information they'll quickly forget after the exam, while teachers feel constrained by rigid curricula that leave no room for innovation. This results in ineffective learning environments.
When schools fail to prioritize creativity in teaching, school becomes boring for both students and teachers, resulting in a lack of shared motivation, excitement, and accomplishment.

slides.notes: A definition brings the reader in and gets everyone agreeing on what we’re talking about. It doesn’t have to be literal ("Dictionary.com defines…"). It can be useful for a term that really needs it, like duality, but warn students not to define what doesn’t need defining: "Dictionary.com defines student as a person who learns." Really?

runs.text: Choose an introduction style that speaks to you and begin your essay:
• Story or example that illustrates your topic
final sentence of your introduction is your thesis statement!

slides.notes: Writing is decision making: this is the moment they decide how to start. On their document, a heading ("Introduction"), and they can paste their thesis below it so they know where they’re heading. Combining styles is fine if it’s intentional; ask students which style they chose as you walk around. Decide your policy on "I": a personal story may need it. They can ask the Tutor for feedback; it won’t write the intro for them, but it may suggest, say, a transition sentence before the thesis.
